title: Quantum Evolution Kernel for Node-Attributed Graphs
authors: Manuel Padovani, Alessandra Di Pierro, Claudia Daffara
abstract: We present a novel approach to embed node-attributed graphs onto neutral-atom quantum computers, and propose an application to digit recognition. Our approach extends PASQAL's quantum evolution kernel (QEK) by introducing a node-level feature encoding based on three-level quantum states. To this purpose, we present a prototype showing how the resulting embedding can be leveraged to extract correlation-based information for classification tasks. The entire quantum process is simulated using Pasqal's Pulser library, which inevitably imposes constraints on the size of the experimental datasets. We compare our method with classical baselines to evaluate its potential. We show that, for the digit recognition task, our method achieves a higher mean accuracy than the more commonly used Jensen-Shannon distance-based methods by utilizing the Wasserstein distance.
summary: This work presents a quantum kernel method to encode node-attributed graphs onto neutral-atom quantum computers for classification. It extends previous quantum evolution kernels by incorporating node features via local Raman laser pulses in a three-level system. The authors demonstrate that using the Wasserstein distance yields strong results, benchmarking the quantum approach against state-of-the-art classical graph neural networks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of embedding node-attributed graphs onto neutral-atom quantum computers for classification tasks like digit recognition.
main_result: The proposed quantum kernel method, utilizing the Wasserstein distance, achieves competitive performance against classical baselines, though the GCN remains the top performer.
method: A novel quantum evolution kernel (QEK) is proposed that extends previous work by encoding node features using local Raman laser rotations in a three-level system.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a neutral-atom quantum computer, modeled using a Hamiltonian incorporating Rydberg blockade interactions ($H_{int}$) and local rotations ($U_{local}$).

important_parameters: The method is designed for the low-data regime, and the kernel comparison favors the Wasserstein distance over the Jensen-Shannon distance.
main_assumptions: The quantum process is simulated using Pasqal's Pulser library, which imposes constraints on the size of the experimental datasets.
figures_summary: Figures compare the performance of the quantum kernel against classical methods (WL, GCN) using different distance metrics, showing Wasserstein distance's superiority over JS distance.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the QEK for graph embedding, details the three-level encoding scheme, compares the Wasserstein distance against other metrics, and evaluates the resulting kernel against classical graph learning models.
why_interesting: It directly applies advanced quantum simulation techniques (Rydberg interactions, local rotations) to a complex data structure (graphs) using quantum machine learning concepts, bridging AMO hardware capabilities with quantum information theory.
